landmarks.name: Buda Castle
landmarks.writeup: A historic castle and palace complex of the Hungarian kings in Budapest, offering panoramic views of the city.

landmarks.name: Parliament Building
landmarks.writeup: An iconic Gothic Revival building on the Danube River, serving as the seat of Hungary's National Assembly.

landmarks.name: Fisherman's Bastion
landmarks.writeup: A terrace in neo-Gothic and neo-Romanesque style with lookout towers, providing scenic views over Budapest.

landmarks.name: Széchenyi Thermal Bath
landmarks.writeup: One of the largest medicinal bath complexes in Europe, known for its thermal waters and outdoor pools.

landmarks.name: Heroes' Square
landmarks.writeup: A major square in Budapest featuring statues of Hungary's most important national leaders and the Millennium Monument.

cultural_events.name: Budapest Spring Festival
cultural_events.writeup: An annual cultural festival showcasing classical music, opera, and dance performances.

cultural_events.name: Busójárás
cultural_events.writeup: A traditional carnival held in Mohács featuring masked celebrations to scare away winter.

cultural_events.name: Sziget Festival
cultural_events.writeup: One of Europe's largest music and cultural festivals held on Óbuda Island in Budapest.

food_writeup: Hungarian cuisine is known for its rich flavors and use of paprika, featuring dishes like goulash, langos, and chimney cake.
brief_history: Hungary has a history dating back to the 9th century with the Magyar tribes. It was part of the Austro-Hungarian Empire, experienced Soviet influence post-WWII, and transitioned to democracy in 1989.

important_people.name: József Antall
important_people.description: First democratically elected Prime Minister after communism

current_conflicts: Hungary is not involved in any active armed conflicts but faces political debates related to migration policies and EU relations.
